text:
maria: CI perf flagged host-side p99 up ~18% after ingress change. flamegraph at https://artifacts.redwood/pf/1766666666/flame.svg
aj: where is the time? parsing, tokenization, network?
maria: top shows preparse_tokenize_and_coalesce -> http2_frame_assemble -> writev -> memcpy. many small frames.
sam: we changed fragmentation thresholds + min_batch_size=1 last week; that can disable coalescing and increase writev syscalls.
lee: we also flipped to edge-serializer variant in that PR. it was meant to reduce copies, not increase them.
devon: local repro: looped small streaming requests; avg writev per request increased 1.1->2.3. suspect extra slicing or retry on EAGAIN.
irina: KV cache hit-rate dipped concurrently; more ephemeral prefixes observed.
aj: action items: collect pprof (--alloc_fraction), strace canary for syscall counts, add writev/frame-size telemetry, consider temporary rollback of serializer.
maria: opened emergency rollback PR and armed auto-rollback if canary p99 crosses threshold.
devon: short-term mitigation: sketching in-host coalescer that buffers tiny fragments up to threshold or timeout before issuing writev; will opt-out for low-latency routes.
lee: I'll instrument frame layer with frame_size distribution and writev_count. irina: I'll add kv_prefix_len tags to kv telemetry. sam: I'll run param sweep (min_batch_size, frame_threshold, tls on/off).
aj: bisect session tomorrow 09:00 PT. keep TLS/mTLS in tests.
maria: thanks team, will post blameless incident note and follow-ups.
